stem:
Imran asks whether 49 is a square number and how to write it with square notation.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: 49 is only a "perfect square" label, not a square number.
Because 49 is a square number it produces a perfect square, so he writes 7 as $49^2$.
49 is a square number because a square array splits into two triangular-number parts.

teacher.key_rationale: 49 is 7 times 7, written $7^2$, so it is a perfect square. Treating "perfect square" as a rival label swaps terms. Writing $49^2$ reverses which number is squared. Triangular split imports another mechanism.
